text:
marta: quick sanity check — I ran a micro-bench for the new quantized model q3b-4q across 3 regions. p50 looks fine but p95 in us-west is much higher than eu-west. wondering if this is an edge-routing issue or kernel mismatch. pasted numbers below. can someone eyeball?

zhang: paste the numbers + how you ran it?

marta: ran 5k short requests (avg length 32 tokens) via our hosted API from each region using the same request stream. basic numbers: 
```
us-east-1  p50=34ms  p95=138ms  throughput=420 qps
us-west-2  p50=48ms  p95=395ms  throughput=390 qps
eu-west-1  p50=66ms  p95=210ms  throughput=375 qps
```
note: model pinned to q3b-4q-2026-03, runtime H100-quant path, kernel set = auto.

leo: that us-west p95 is suspicious. did the requests route through a different edge/proxy hop? route-bot, any recent rota changes?

route-bot: detected 18% increase in average proxy hops for us-west during the run window (1711009800-1711009950). Details: avg_hops us-west=4.1, us-east=2.3, eu-west=2.9

anita: also check KV cache warmup for that run. if requests are colder in us-west you'll see higher tail. how long between warmup and measurement?

marta: good call — no explicit warmup, tests from fresh clients spread across AZs. warmup likely inconsistent.

sam: two quick things to triage: 1) run a controlled curl loop to a specific edge ip to isolate routing variance; 2) force kernel=stable-optimized to rule out an auto kernel pick bug.

zhang: +1. also include --streaming=false for the baseline; streaming can add tail if proxy buffers differ.

marta: repro commands I used: 
```
for r in us-east-1 us-west-2 eu-west-1; do 
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
    -d '{"model":"q3b-4q-2026-03","input":"hi","max_tokens":32}' | jq '.latency_ms'
done
```

leo: if you get consistent hop delta then capacity sizing might be off (extra proxy hops add serialization). what's the per-GPU batch size and CPU worker count on the us-west serving fleet?

marta: us-west pool config (from console): GPU batch target 128, batch_timeout 12ms, CPU workers 28. us-east/ eu-west same config.

anita: could be a networking egress queue in one of the us-west edge routers. ask infra to dump interface io stats for the node group used during the run.

sam: also be mindful of quant runtime path — the H100-quant path recently had a patch that changes GEMM kernel selection under certain sequence lengths. if us-west saw a different sequence-length distribution (more long tokens) auto kernel could pick slower kernel and inflate p95. check runtime logs for kernel decisions.

zhang: where are those logs? I can grep the inference-agent logs for kernel.selection entries if you share the job id.

marta: job id 2026-03-q3b-4q-smoke-1711009. infra logs: 
```
[2026-03-10 12:31:02] kernel.selection: model=q3b-4q variant=4q quant=8 kernel=gemm_ndc_v2 seq=16
[2026-03-10 12:33:45] kernel.selection: model=q3b-4q variant=4q quant=8 kernel=gemm_ndc_v3 seq=64
```

leo: that v3/GEMM pickup at seq=64 could slow tail if some requests spike to longer seqs. do you have token length histogram per-region?

marta: brief hist: us-east median=28 mean=31 99th=112; us-west median=30 mean=37 99th=210; eu-west median=33 mean=35 99th=128. so us-west has heavier right tail.

anita: aha — combined: extra proxy hops + longer seq tail + kernel switch = compounding p95 inflation. fix plan: 1) add a short warmup phase in us-west to pre-populate KV cache; 2) pin kernel to gemm_ndc_v2 for a test cohort; 3) route some traffic to local-edge via routing policy to drop proxy hops and measure delta.

sam: we should also run a small A/B: 50% pinned kernel v2 + route-local-edge, 50% auto+control. look at p50/p95 and token-cost delta. can we schedule a canary in the next 20m?

marta: yes i can kick off a canary. starting in 10m: 2k requests per region, include warmup. will post numbers here.

(10m later)

marta: quick canary results: 
```
us-west control  p50=47ms p95=389ms
us-west pinned-kernel+local-edge p50=42ms p95=172ms
eu-west control  p50=65ms p95=215ms
eu-west pinned-kernel+local-edge p50=62ms p95=198ms
```

leo: nice. big improvement on us-west p95. suggests routing hop reduction was primary, kernel pinning helped too.

zhang: can you open a tiny runbook item for: 1) ensure warmup sequence for new model onboarding; 2) flag if region seq-99 > 150 tokens during onboarding; 3) default kernel pin for first canary?

anita: I'll add infra check to surface avg proxy hops per region in the console (quick graph).

sam: follow-ups: investigate why us-west edge had more hops (deployment timing, DNS failover?), and upstream of that check if our router mesh introduced another proxy.

marta: thanks all — I'll capture the canary artifacts into the model-onboarding ticket and mark next steps. :thumbsup:
